items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: He knew how to find the right arrangers for his music. The Bill Holmans, the Gerry Mulligans, the Bill Russos

ctx.x: we had in 1955 where Bill Holman was writing. and then it started to lean towards the swing/ jazz thing and they had great soloists — Charlie Mariano, Lenny Niehaus, Frank Rosolino and Carl Fontana and there was a lot of good soloists on the band. And then the band leaned a little bit more toward jazz. But actually, Stan wasn’t really a jazz kind of person or musician. He just wanted interesting music. And it leaned toward jazz.

Yeah. He was an organizer and he presented and provided a vehicle for the players and the arrangers. He knew how to find the right arrangers for his music. The Bill Holmans, the Gerry Mulligans, the Bill Russos, Bill, I mean what’s his name, Johnny—
Richards, the “Cuban Fire” album, which is a collector’s item.
